answer: Put \(N=\binom n2\), \(B=2^N+1\), and \(Q=\operatorname{lcm}(1,2,\ldots,n^{n-2})\). For each \(0\le k<2^N\), define the symmetric matrix \(A(k)=(a_{ij})\) by \(a_{ii}=0\) and, for \(i<j\), \[p(i,j)=\frac{(i-1)(2n-i)}2+j-i-1,\qquad a_{ij}=a_{ji}=\left\lfloor\frac{k}{2^{p(i,j)}}\right\rfloor-2\left\lfloor\frac{k}{2^{p(i,j)+1}}\right\rfloor.\] Set \(d_i=\sum_j a_{ij}\), \(L=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)-A(k)\), \(T=\det L[\{1,\ldots,n-1\}]\), and \(F=\det L[\{1,\ldots,n-2\}]\), where \(L[I]\) denotes a principal submatrix. Define \[z=\left\lfloor\frac1{1+T}\right\rfloor,\qquad \rho=\prod_{i=1}^{n-1}\left\lfloor\frac1{1+(d_i-d_n)^2}\right\rfloor,\qquad E=\frac{Q(d_1+\cdots+d_n)F}{T+z}.\] Then the explicit exact formula is \[\boxed{t_n=\frac1Q\left\lfloor\log_B\left(\sum_{k=0}^{2^N-1}(1-z)\rho B^E\right)\right\rfloor.}\] This enumerative formula holds throughout the stated domain, indeed for every \(n\ge2\).
